articles.title: Serbian President Vucic criticizes Kosovo war crimes verdict
articles.summary: The conviction of four former Kosovo Liberation Army leaders has drawn sharply different reactions across the Balkans. Serbia has accused the court of failing to fully address crimes against Serbs.

image.caption: Former Kosovo President Hashim Thaci (pictured here in court in The Hague in 2023) was sentenced to 25 years in prison on WednesdayImage: Koen van Weel/ANP/AFP

blocks.text: The Kosovo war crimes tribunal in The Hague on Wednesday found four former leaders of the Kosovo Liberation Army (KLA) guilty of war crimes committed during the 1998–99 Kosovo war.

The war was fought between the forces of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia and Serbia, on the one side, and the KLA on the other, and took place in the context of the breakup of the former Yugoslavia.

Former Kosovo President Hashim Thaci and former KLA leaders Kadri Veseli, Rexhep Selimi and Jakup Krasniqi were sentenced at first instance by the Kosovo Specialist Chambers to a combined 81 years in prison: Thaci and Krasniqi to 25 years each, Veseli to 18 and Selimi to 13 years.
The four men were convicted of the arbitrary detention of 385 people, cruel treatment of 49 people, torture of 303 people and the murder of 96 people.
They were acquitted of the charges of crimes against humanity on the grounds that it had not been proven that there had been a widespread or systematic attack directed against a civilian population.
Vucic: Court 'did not want to undermine KLA's credibility'

Speaking at a press conference on Wednesday evening, Serbian President Aleksandar Vucic criticized the fact that the Kosovo Specialist Chambers (which is part of Kosovo's judicial system but is based in The Hague and staffed by international judges) did not convict the four former KLA leaders of crimes against humanity.

blocks.caption: Vucic criticized the ruling by the Kosovo Specialist Chambers on WednesdayImage: Filip Stevanovic/Anadolu/picture alliance

blocks.text: "As a court of the so-called Kosovo, they did not want to undermine the credibility of the KLA and did not address the merits of the matter concerning the formation of forces aimed at seceding Kosovo from Serbia and the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia," he said.

Vucic added that the verdict did not cover crimes committed against Serbs after June 20, 1999, when KFOR, an international peacekeeping mission led by NATO, arrived in Kosovo after the armed conflict had officially ended.
'United in hatred against Serbs'
Vucic had strong words on the reactions to the verdict from several states of the former Yugoslavia.

Commenting on Kosovo Prime Minister Albin Kurti's assessment that the verdict represented an "unacceptable injustice," Vucic said: "Imagine if we had said that about any defendant or convicted person. How many resolutions and declarations would various European and world parliaments have adopted against our people and our country?"

This was an allusion to the condemnation by European officials of the funeral last week of former Bosnian Serb commander and convicted war criminal Ratko Mladic, which was attended by large numbers of citizens and several Serbian government ministers in Belgrade.
Hague tribunal convicts Hashim Thaci of Kosovo war crimes

Vucic also commented on a statement issued by Croatia's Ministry of Foreign and European Affairs, which said the verdict did not change the fact that the people of Kosovo had been victims of repression and crimes committed by Serbian leader Slobodan Milosevic's regime.
"There are no Serbs as victims; in every statement, Serbs have to be the perpetrators," said Vucic. "All of them in the region are united in hatred against Serbs."
Individualization of criminal responsibility
Serbian lawyer Aleksandar Olenik, who works on war crimes cases in the former Yugoslavia, gave a positive assessment of the ruling.

"It is well known that war crimes were committed in the territory of Kosovo that was under the control of the KLA during the 1990s. We now have judgments and the individualization of criminal responsibility," he told DW.

blocks.caption: Serbian lawyer Aleksandar Olenik said that the respect shown for victims in the proceedings in The Hague represents 'progress in international criminal law'Image: Media Center in Belgrade

blocks.text: Olenik pointed out that the respect shown for victims in the proceedings in The Hague represents "progress in international criminal law."
"In previous ad hoc tribunals, victims were merely witnesses, merely a means of proving guilt. At this court, they have their own legal representative and are entitled to compensation," he said.
More trials to come in Kosovo?
Olenik explained that in accordance with the Kosovo law that established the Kosovo Specialist Chambers, only the founders of the KLA are subject to prosecution before that court.
Kosovo's domestic judiciary will prosecute other members of the organization believed to have committed crimes.

blocks.caption: There was shock and disbelief in Kosovo after the verdict was announcedImage: Ermal Meta/Matrix Images/IMAGO

blocks.text: "The summary of the judgment names individuals who were not included in the indictment but who were found to have committed criminal offenses," he said. "It is now up to the other part of Kosovo's judicial system to prosecute, first, those against whom evidence was presented in these proceedings, and then others as well. This should also cover the period after the end of the armed conflict, that is, after June 20, 1999."
Serbia, Kosovo 'heighten the potential for conflict'

Stasa Zajovic of Women in Black, a Belgrade-based NGO founded in the early 1990s that is primarily engaged in anti-war activities, said neither the "Serbian regime nor the Kosovo authorities" use judgments in war crimes cases "to examine their own responsibility in the war, but rather to heighten the potential for conflict."

"When I say that they use similar patterns, I cannot equate the scale of the crimes committed by the two sides. It must not be forgotten that the Serbian regime is responsible for the largest number of atrocities in the territory of the former Yugoslavia, particularly in Kosovo," she told DW.
Speaking about tensions in Kosovo following the pronouncement of the verdict in The Hague on Wednesday, Zajovic said "it is important that international forces are present to monitor the situation."

blocks.caption: Disbelief soon turned to anger in Pristina as protesters clashed with riot police outside the headquarters of the European Union Rule of Law Mission in KosovoImage: Valdrin Xhemaj/REUTERS

blocks.text: "It is clear that the conditions do not exist for armed conflict, but there is a danger that the war could continue by other means," she said.
Future impact of the verdict
Asked how the verdict would affect relations between Serbia and Kosovo, lawyer Olenik recalled that previous judgments by international courts have had little impact in this regard.
"I hope things will be better now. That depends on the political elites in both countries," he said, adding that Kosovo society "has been pushed considerably to the right over the past four years."

"I am not optimistic that the verdict will have a positive effect in the near future," he said. "But I think that, as time passes — in 10 or 15 years — people will look at what has been established by these judgments in a more realistic manner and without such strong emotions."

articles.title: Impeachment court issues show cause order on Ridon, Tolosa over sub judice rule
articles.summary: The Senate impeachment court issued a show cause order on House prosecutor Terry Ridon and private prosecutor Benjamin Tolosa, Jr., asking them to explain their statements that could violate the sub…

blocks.text: Published September 17, 2026 7:13pm

The Senate impeachment court issued a show cause order on House prosecutor Terry Ridon and private prosecutor Benjamin Tolosa, Jr., asking them to explain their statements that could violate the sub judice rule, meaning the ban on parties from discussing the merits of the impeachment case against Vice President Sara Duterte outside the trial proceedings.

This was confirmed by Ridon to reporters on Thursday, a day after the Senate impeachment court announced the issuance of the show cause orders on two members of the prosecution panel without naming names.

“We confirm that we received the show cause order from the Senate impeachment court concerning sub judice matters. We respect the decision of the Impeachment court, and we will answer the order by the end of today,” Ridon told reporters at the sidelines of the ongoing budget briefing.
“Aside from me, Atty. Tolosa was also given a show cause order, and he will also answer it by the end of the day,” Ridon added.

The sub judice rule is provided under Article 18 of the Rules on Impeachment, which states that the presiding officer, the members of the Senate, “shall refrain from making any comments and disclosures in public pertaining to the merits of a pending impeachment trial” and that “the same shall likewise apply to the prosecutors, the person impeached, and their respective counsel and witnesses.”

Senate impeachment court presiding officer Francis Escudero, back in August 2026, cautioned the parties against violating the sub judice rule by saying that violations going forward will have consequences, including a P30,000 fine per offense.
Ridon did not cite the specific statements that were flagged by the Senate impeachment court.
Instead, he stressed that it was the prosecutors’ duty to explain the impeachment process to the public within the rules set by the Impeachment court.

“Our role as prosecutors should be viewed in the entirety of the context of explaining to the public the goings-on of the trial. We have never asked the court to pre-judge. The impeachment trial is ongoing,” Ridon said.

“We do not seek to influence the senator-judges. Ultimately, ang pinakamahalaga po, hindi lang po kami-kami sa kapulungan. Ang pinakamahalaga po, nauunawaan ng ordinaryong Pilipino kung bakit kung meron po tayong paglilitis, bakit mahalaga po yung katotohanan, bakit mahalaga yung pananagutan,” Ridon added.

(The understanding of the process should not be limited to the members of Congress. The most important thing here is for the Filipino people to understand why there is a trial, why the truth matters, and why accountability is important.)
Ridon, however, said the prosecution will submit to the decision of the impeachment court.

“Whatever these statements [supposedly violating sub judice], we leave it to the court to make that determination. We don't want to debate with the court because they are the court,” Ridon added. —LDF, GMA News

articles.title: King Charles, Earl Spencer clash over Diana death once again
articles.summary: Buckingham Palace has rejected criticisms of King Charles III in a new book from the brother of his late wife Princess Diana. Earl Charles Spencer has been a fierce critic of his former…

image.caption: The feud between King Charles and Earl Charles Spencer, Princess Diana's brother, dates back to her death and funeral in 1997 — as do the latest allegations in Spencer's new bookImage: Gerry Penny/dpa/picture alliance

blocks.text: Buckingham Palace has hit back at claims by the late Princess Diana's brother that King Charles III acted cruelly after her death in a car crash in 1997 — the latest of many criticisms leveled at the king by his former brother-in-law Earl Charles Spencer in recent decades.
The dispute is liable to overshadow a public engagement on Thursday when Charles will meet with various AI executives in Scotland to appeal to them to take care in their work.
What is the argument about?

Earl Spencer, Diana's elder brother, has written a new book being serialized in the Daily Mail newspaper, in which he alleges that Charles told him in an angry phone call, "rest assured, we'll forget her soon enough," days after Diana died aged 36.

"While we do not comment on books as a matter of principle, His Majesty is mindful that the pain of fraternal grief can cloud reason, affect judgment and color memory in ways others do not recognize, even many years after such a loss," a palace spokesperson said late on Wednesday.
Charles and Diana had gone through an acrimonious separation prior to her death in 1997 and relations between the two Charles' were already at rock bottom prior to the late-night tragedy in Paris.

blocks.caption: Charles Spencer resides at the family estate Althrop House in NorthamptonshireImage: Jordan Pettitt/empics/picture alliance

blocks.text: In the book, "Swan Song: Diana, My Sister," which is due to be published in full next week, Spencer repeats his assertion that he called for Princes William and Harry — then aged 15 and 12 — not to walk in the massive public funeral procession for their mother on September 6, 1997.
Spencer claims that Charles subjected him to a "stream of anger" after he raised this objection.

"He unleashed down the phone what I have always taken to be his pent-up contempt for Diana, and his horror that the world was so bowled over by her death. 'Rest assured', he hissed, 'we'll forget her soon enough!'," Spencer writes.

Diana's sudden death in a car crash as her chauffeur tried to evade paparazzi photographers led to an outpouring of grief in much of the UK and beyond for the popular if polarizing princess — known for her striking looks, a relatively easy manner by royal standards, and for her engagement with charitable causes. The monarchy faced accusations of failing to adequately respond in public to her death, particularly in the immediate aftermath.
The feud between the Spencers and the Windsors both before and particularly after her death has been a recurring feature in the British press and on popular TV shows like Netflix's "The Crown."

blocks.caption: Diana died a few months after this photo was taken, aged 36Image: John Stillwell/PA Wire/empics/picture alliance

blocks.text: Charles and Camilla in Scotland, set for AI event
Charles and Queen consort Camilla have been at Balmoral Castle in Scotland for most of September, attending a series of appointments amid their stay.

One of the higher profile engagements takes place on Thursday at Dumfries House in Ayrshire, where Charles is hosting executives from AI companies like Nvidia, Google DeepMind, Open AI and Anthropic, among others, at what's seen as a crucial time for the industry.

"The decisions taken at this ​formative time ‌will shape the world inherited by future generations," the King would say, according to excerpts released in advance by the palace. "The task before you is not merely to advance technology, but to ensure that it remains firmly in the service of humanity, community and the natural world."
Britain's Minister for Artificial Intelligence Kanishka Narayan, promoted to a new bespoke ministerial role by new Prime Minister Andy Burnham, will also attend the event.
So will Paolo Benanti, an adviser to Pope Leo XIV, who has demonstrated considerable interest, and indeed concern, in AI development.

Former Philippine President Rodrigo Duterte appears at the International Criminal Court (ICC) in The Hague on September 16, 2026, during a preparatory session as he faces charges over his “war on drugs,” which killed thousands.

MANILA, Philippines — Malacañang said former President Rodrigo Duterte appears to be in good shape at the International Criminal Court (ICC) following his first in-person appearance on Wednesday, September 16.
Palace Press Officer Claire Castro gave the Palace’s comment on Duterte’s appearance in a press briefing on Thursday, September 17.

“Unang-una sa mga kababayan natin, nakita naman po natin na maganda naman po ang kalagayan ng ating dating pangulo na si dating Pangulong Duterte. At nakita naman po natin na mukhang accepted naman niya po na magtuloy-tuloy ang hearing sa ICC. So yun lamang po,” Castro said.
(First of all, to our countrymen, we saw that former President Duterte seems to be in good condition. And he appeared to have accepted that the ICC trial would proceed. That’s all.)

The former president’s defense team previously claimed that he is mentally unfit to participate in the proceedings and that his condition continues to deteriorate, preventing him from retaining information and accessing memories.
Duterte, who preceded President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. as president, made his first in-person appearance at Wednesday’s status hearing on his case.
He faces three counts of crimes against humanity over his alleged involvement in 76 murders during his war on drugs.
Before Wednesday’s appearance, Duterte initially appeared via online teleconference after his arrest in March 2025.

The pictograms in the Codex Boturini narrate the story of the migration of the Aztecs, also known as Mexica, from their ancestral homeland to the shores of Lake Texcoco, where they built Tenochtitlán.
The temporary exchange of the two codices was agreed by Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum and her French counterpart, Emmanuel Macron, during a visit by the latter to Mexico last year.
Mexico has long lobbied for the return of historical artefacts taken from the country in past centuries.
According to Mexico's ministry of foreign relations, last year more than 2,000 objects were successfully repatriated.

articles.title: ‘So many loopholes’: Democratic House leader Jeffries flags concerns over Russia sanctions bill – US politics live
articles.summary:
Jeffries said the legislation had ​so many loopholes that sanctions harming Russia might not be applied

The unprecedented spate of mid-decade redistricting for the US House has…

blocks.text: Key events

items: 34m agoDemocratic House leader Jeffries flags concerns as House passes Russia sanctions bill

blocks.text: The unprecedented spate of mid-decade redistricting for the US House has changed the congressional districts for one-tenth of Americans and significantly altered the makeup of at least one-fifth of districts, according to a new study.
A report by Protect Democracy found that 34.8m people - about one in 10 Americans - now live in a different district than they did during the 2024 election cycle.
And about one-fifth of all Americans now live in a district where more than a quarter of voters are new to the district compared with the last election cycle, AP reported.
The findings display the stark overhaul that partisan redistricting fights kicked off by president Donald Trump last year have caused for Americans across the country.

“If this trend continues, it really brings into question whether or not elected officials are really representing their constituents anymore, or if the voters are being randomly picked by mapmakers to squeeze out partisan advantage,” said Ben Raderstorf, a policy advocate at Protect Democracy and one of the paper’s co-authors.
Democratic House leader Jeffries flags concerns as House passes Russia sanctions bill
Hello and welcome to the US politics live blog.

House Democratic leader Hakeem Jeffries said the Russia sanctions bill had “so many loopholes” as Congress passed the sweeping bill to give Donald Trump the power to raise tariffs on top buyers of Russian energy.

The Lindsey O Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026 passed in a 262-159 vote on the last day before Congress goes on recess ahead of the midterm elections. Graham, who died earlier this year, co-authored and submitted the bill more than a year and a half ago.
But Jeffries said the legislation had ​so many loopholes that sanctions harming Russia might not be applied.
“What ​this legislation will do is give Donald Trump, perhaps, unfettered authority to unleash tariffs on the American people,” the New York lawmaker said as he announced he ​would vote no.
He added:
double quotation markWhy in the world would this Congress give this president additional authority to visit that kind of economic harm on the American people?

The bill would mandate new sanctions on Russian political and military officials, and foreign networks helping to supply Russia’s war machine and evade existing sanctions. It would also target Russia’s so-called fleet of “shadow tankers”, which have allowed the country to continue to ship crude around the world despite sanctions on its energy exports.
It would also allow Trump to impose tariffs of up to 100% on the top purchasers of Russian energy, including China, as well as other countries helping the Kremlin evade sanctions.

Democratic staffers supporting the bill said that it offered a “last chance” to increase sanctions on Russia before Ukraine entered a “long winter”. Russia has improved the drone technology it has used to strike Ukrainian infrastructure as Kyiv has suffered a shortage of anti-air missiles, leaving the country in a dire position.
Don Bacon, a Nebraska Republican supporting the bill, called it the US Congress’ “Churchill vs Chamberlain Moment on Russia”.
Read our full report here:
In other developments:

items: Donald Trump responded to the Federal Reserve’s unanimous decision on Wednesday to raise its benchmark interest rate by a quarter-percentage point, to a range of 3.75% to 4%, by demanding a massive cut in rates.

Asked why it is so important to him to have his name inscribed on the Kennedy Center, a memorial to another president, Trump said he deserves “recognition” for saving the venue. If not, Trump said, “It’ll end up being ripped down.
Congresswoman Joyce Beatty, a Democrat and Kennedy Center trustee, has filed a motion for an emergency hearing on the performing arts venue’s apparent closure.

Mitch McConnell, the former Republican Senate majority leader who returned to work this week after a months‑long absence, had to be prompted by colleagues as to how to vote near the start of a televised meeting of the Senate agriculture committee on Wednesday.

The House speaker, Mike Johnson, cancelled votes currently scheduled for Thursday, meaning that lower chamber lawmakers will now head back to their districts for the midterm recess a day early. The change to schedule means that the House will avoid voting on Republican congressman Thomas Massie’s resolution to impeach the defense secretary, Pete Hegseth.

Speaking in North Carolina, Trump explicitly compared his effort to blame Democrat Roy Cooper, the former governor and Senate candidate, for the brutal killing of a young Ukrainian refugee, Iryna Zarutska, last year, by using false information, on the infamous 1988 Willie Horton ad.

articles.title: U.S. House closes until the midterms after Republican brings resolution to impeach Hegseth
articles.summary: U.S. Speaker Mike Johnson closed up the House early, sending lawmakers home Wednesday to campaign for the midterm elections after what he claims is the most productive Congress in decades.

image.caption: U.S. House Speaker Mike Johnson talks to reporters outside of his office on Capitol Hill in Washington on Wednesday. (Mariam Zuhaib/The Associated Press)

blocks.text: World
U.S. Speaker Mike Johnson closed up the House early, sending lawmakers home Wednesday to campaign for the midterm elections after what he claims is the most productive Congress in decades.
U.S. House was in session for just 7 days after returning from summer break

The decision came after just seven days in session following a summer break. It led to a scathing rebuke from a member of his own party, Rep. Thomas Massie, of Kentucky, who brought a resolution the previous day to impeach Secretary of War Pete Hegseth over the war in Iran.
"We're calling off Congress? And we're in the majority?" Massie railed from the House floor.

Johnson, of Louisiana, has repeatedly and abruptly cancelled House voting days to send lawmakers home rather than manage the disruptions from his own rebellious flank, particularly those legislative efforts that threatened to rebuke U.S. President Donald Trump.

By one tally, the House has cut 28 days this year, while adding four others, for a net loss of 24 days — about one-fourth of the total scheduled — for one of the shortest sessions for the chamber in modern times.
Johnson's decision led to criticism from another Republican, Rep. Ralph Norman, of South Carolina.
"The House has now cancelled at least 63 scheduled voting days this Congress, including nine days this month alone, and now we're leaving Washington until after the election," Norman wrote on X.
"The founders did not envision taking this much time off and still getting paid."
LISTEN | David Smith, the Guardian's Washington bureau chief, on Hegseth's rise:
Front Burner30:05Pete Hegseth: the Iran war’s chief promoter
Speaker dismisses Massie's 'stunt'

Massie seized control of the chamber for a blistering hour-long speech criticizing Johnson, the Republican majority and the work he said the speaker is refusing to conduct to lower prices for Americans and hold the Trump administration accountable.
"Why would we be cancelling days when the country is burning?" Massie said. "We should stay here for every day that's on the calendar and we should debate."
Johnson insisted "the House has done its job."
The Republican speaker tallied the hundreds of bills passed by the House this session and, as lawmakers bolted for the exits, said they are on a 48-hour notice to return to Washington if needed.

On Wednesday, the House powered through a full agenda, passing bills large and small — including a sweeping bill to impose sanctions on Russia over the war in Ukraine, and another to name the American mastodon the national fossil mammal and the Tyrannosaurus Rex the national fossil dinosaur.
"We're walking out here with our heads high," he said.
Earlier in the day, he dismissed Massie's effort to impeach Hegseth as "a stunt."
"Secretary Hegseth has done an extraordinary job at the Department of War," Johnson said.

items: Several U.S. military bases, diplomatic buildings have been damaged in Iran war: inspector general report
Canada restricts drug boat intel from U.S. navy's Caribbean airstrike operation

blocks.text: Despite the enormous tools of the gavel — the speaker holds one of the most powerful positions in Washington, second in the line of succession to the president — Johnson has often been thwarted by his own conference in the past two years.

Voters will be assessing the situation in November as they decide whether to keep Trump's party in power, while Democrats work to dislodge Republicans from majority control of both the House and the Senate.
Massie cites Iran, deadly attacks on boats
House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries assailed the Republicans for "have done nothing to make life more affordable for the American people."

The confrontation also provided a platform for Massie, the libertarian-leaning, go-his-own-way congressman who was instrumental in pushing for the Epstein Files Transparency Act while also helping lead efforts to end the conflict in Iran through a war powers resolution.

The moves were a thorn for Johnson and the Trump administration, and Massie lost his own primary bid for re-election after Trump mounted a costly campaign to kick him out of Congress, with Hegseth among those who hit the campaign trail to endorse the Kentuckian's opponent, former Navy SEAL Ed Gallrein.
CBC speaks to a former adviser to the U.S. Department of State on the strikes on alleged drug boats
Massie on Wednesday devoted substantial time to criticizing Hegseth and the "stupid war" he said the U.S. should not be involved with in Iran.

Earlier this week, an inspector general report laid out the costs through four months of the war, which included damage and destruction to several U.S. military bases and diplomatic stations, as well as a drawdown of limited weapons systems and munitions.

Hegseth's role in sending the U.S. into the Iran wars without approval of Congress and directing the U.S.'s military strikes of alleged drug trafficking boats in the Caribbean are among the actions Massie characterized as high crimes and misdemeanours in the articles of impeachment against the war secretary.
With files from CBC New

articles.title: MV June Aster communication system failed before fire warning, says captain
articles.summary: MV June Aster captain said the fire incident happened so quickly.

blocks.text: September 17, 2026 | 6:30pm

MANILA, Philippines — The captain of MV June Aster, which caught fire off Coron, Palawan, said that the vessel’s communication system failed due to a blackout, preventing him from alerting the passengers about the tragedy.
The captain, identified as Roel Sarmiento, recalled the series of events before and after the fire incident on September 9 in a sworn statement he submitted to authorities.

In a copy obtained by ABS-CBN News, Sarmiento said he immediately went to the ferry’s very high frequency (VHF) radio and public-address system to warn the passengers after he noticed that the fire was quickly spreading on the right side of the ship, but was not able to do so because the power went out.

“Sumilip ako sa starboard wing, nakita ko buong kanan na bahagi ng barko ay napakalakas ng apoy, pati sa kaliwa tanaw ko. Dali-dali akong pumunta sa Very High Frequency (VHF) at sa Public Address (PA) para makapag-inform kaso biglang nagka-black out na,” Sarmiento said.

(I looked out from the starboard wing, I saw that the whole right side of the ship was engulfed in flames, and I could see it even on the left side. I immediately went to the Very High Frequency and Public Address to inform, but there was suddenly a blackout.)
On September 12, the Philippine Coast Guard (PCG) recovered 41 charred remains from the ship.
Authorities said 77 people died, 43 survived and 12 remain missing. A total of 128 passengers were aboard the ship.
‘Jump, captain’
Sarmiento said in his statement that he boarded the ship on September 8 at 9:32 a.m. at Baseco, Manila. The loading of rolling cargo began at 7:15 p.m., and the ship sailed at 8:14 p.m.
They experienced subasko, or a squall, while approaching Hamilo Point near Corregidor Traffic Separation Scheme. The seas improved as they got closer to Fortune Island.
The whole day of September 9 was fine until 6:29 p.m., when one of his crew members informed him that a fire had broken out.

“Ang naisagot ko ay ‘saan’, at direkta kong sinabi na papasukin ang mga pasahero sa bridge at buksan ang pinto. Tapos sinabi ko sa AB (able seaman) na prepare ang hose ng tubig at fire extinguisher,” Sarmiento said.
(I answered, ‘where’, and I directly told them to get the passengers inside the bridge and open the door. Then I told the AB to prepare the water hose and fire extinguisher.)

When he looked from the starboard wing, he saw that the fire was quickly spreading on the right side of the vessel. The fire was also visible on the left side. That was when he tried to warn the passengers through the public-address system, but failed.
Sarmiento said that he then ordered the crew to deploy the life rafts since they no longer had any choice but to abandon the ship.
After two life rafts were deployed, he instructed some of the passengers to jump out of the ship. He said they even helped a mother who could not climb over the railings out of fear.

When the passengers and crew got out of the ship, Sarmiento said he removed his shirt, soaked it, and used it to cover his face as he attempted to open the air-conditioned room to check if there were any passengers trapped inside.
But the heat became unbearable, and when he looked out from the right side of the ship’s wing, the passengers and crew told him to jump out of the burning ship.
“Tinawag nila ako na “talon na Kap, talon na”” he said. (They called me, and said 'just jump Captain, jump.')
‘Things happened quickly’
Sarmiento said he had no choice but to wear his shirt and jump out of the ship, even without a life jacket, because of the unbearable heat.
“About 30 meters ang layo ko sa isang AB at nasambit ko na pahawak sa lifejacket n'ya at ako ay nahihirapan na,” he recalled.
(I am about 30 meters away from an AB, and I asked him if I could hold on to his life jacket because I was already having difficulty.”)
The seaman then took off the life jacket he was wearing and gave it to Sarmiento, who then swam toward a life raft.
Sarmiento was then able to get on the raft, together with three crew members and two passengers. They paddled until they were rescued by fishermen who brought them to shore.
He said he was in tears when they reached the shore, thinking that he was not able to do anything to stop the fire.

“Sa sobrang trauma ko ay naglakad lang po ako nang naglakad sa kalsada hanggang sa makarating ako kung saan man. Hanggang ngayon, isip pa din ako nang isip kung paano naging sobrang bilis ng pangyayari,” Sarmiento said.
(I was so traumatized that I just walked and walked along the road until I reached somewhere. Until now, I’m still thinking how quickly things happened.)
Sarmiento went missing after the incident and turned up after five days.

articles.title: Team Japan forced to look at alternate accommodation options at home Asian Games
articles.summary: Abandoning plans to set up an Athletes' Village, 2026 Asian Games host Nagoya sets up alternative accommodation options, including a chartered cruise ship and shipping-container style huts

blocks.text: ATHLETES' UNITS. A person walks near wooden container units built to house athletes, including those for Japanese and Filipino athletes, ahead of the Aichi-Nagoya 2026 Asian Games in Nagoya, Japan.
Edgar Su/REUTERS
Abandoning plans to set up an Athletes' Village, 2026 Asian Games host Nagoya sets up alternative accommodation options, including a chartered cruise ship and shipping-container style huts

items: Accommodation issues have arisen for the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games, with athletes facing mixed-gender room assignments and delays in entry procedures.
Local organizers opted for creative housing solutions, including a cruise ship and shipping-container huts, due to an unexpected increase in participant numbers.
The organizing committee is committed to addressing complaints and improving living conditions for athletes, while also preparing backup accommodations in case of further challenges.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.

NAGOYA, Japan – Accommodation issues continued to plague the lead-up to the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games on Thursday, September 17, with even the host Japan team looking at alternative arrangements after cases in which male and female athletes were allocated shared rooms.

Local organizers, having decided not to build a dedicated Athletes’ Village, looked to creative accommodation options to house the 17,000 competitors and officials arriving for the Games, which officially open on Saturday, September 19 .

The Italian cruise ship Costa Serena, which will host 4,000 participants, arrived on Tuesday, September 15, and 2,000 other athletes and officials will be accommodated in shipping-container style huts in the dock area of Japan’s biggest port.

“Since the cruise ship village opened yesterday, athletes have been arriving and going through the entry procedures,” Japan’s deputy chef de mission Hisashi Mizutori told a news conference on Thursday.
“However, the process took a significant amount of time, and due to issues with activation of their credentials, we have received reports that some athletes were left waiting for several hours.

“There have been cases where coaches, team officials, and athletes have been assigned to the same room. There are also situations where room assignments were made purely based on the numbers, such as assigning five twin rooms for a group of five men and five women.

“While the numbers match on paper, practically it creates challenging situations such as men and women being assigned together, coaches being assigned with athletes, or trainers who need to accommodate a lot of medical equipment being assigned together.”

The local organizing committee maintains that the accommodation issue arose because they were expecting 15,000 athletes and officials for the Games, only for numbers to increase as new sports were added.

In a joint statement with the Olympic Council of Asia (OCA) last week, the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games Organizing Committee said numbers would be capped at 17,000 with all of those guaranteed a place to stay.
Mizutori said the Japanese Olympic Committee (JOC) had anticipated accommodation “challenges” and had secured hotel rooms in the city as a backup.
“We heard that the accommodation allocations are extremely tight,” said the former Olympic champion gymnast, who also sits on the JOC executive board.

“We are currently working to coordinate and negotiate adjustments wherever possible. For cases where that proves too difficult, we are considering using the backup accommodations that Team Japan prepared in advance as alternatives.”
Last Tuesday, Asian Games organizers said they were committed to addressing complaints from athletes and officials about accommodation.

There have been media reports of complaints from South Korean basketball players about the size of the beds in the shipping container-style huts on land that will be home to some 2,000 of the visitors.
“We are fully aware of the dissatisfaction and concerns voiced by the athlete delegations,” accommodation manager Yuta Matsuo told Reuters.
“However, we are not merely acknowledging these issues, we are already taking concrete steps to improve the environment for the athletes, including their living conditions during their stay.”

Matsuo said the core concept of the accommodation program had been sustainability and that while everything had been approved by the Japanese Olympic Committee, he understood that other delegations would have specific needs.
A resident center operating 24 hours a day would be available to address any complaints or problems from athletes or officials, Matsuo said.
“In this way, we are making every effort to ensure that athletes do not have to remain anxious or worried for prolonged periods of time,” he said.
Matsuo suggested that some of the cabins on the Costa Serena might be quite small but urged athletes to make the most of the extensive shared space on the ship.
“We hope the delegation will consider the ship’s facilities and relaxation options — taking a comprehensive view rather than focusing solely on cabin size,” he said.

The local organizing committee maintains that the accommodation issue arose because they were expecting only 15,000 athletes and officials for the Games, only for numbers to increase as new sports were added.
In a joint statement with the Olympic Council of Asia last week, the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games Organizing Committee said numbers would be capped at 17,000 with all of those guaranteed a place to stay.
The weather has not helped with several hundred athletes and officials briefly evacuated from their accommodation after torrential rain battered Nagoya last week.
The Games, the third edition to be held in Japan, will run from Saturday until October 4. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Canada's Carney welcomes associate status idea in EU speech
articles.summary: Mark Carney wants to strengthen Canada's ties to the European Union amid a growing rift with the US under Donald Trump. The US president has threatened to halt trade with Europe if it makes Canada an…

image.caption: Should the Canadian parliament approve the plan, Canada would become the EU's first 'associate' memberImage: Yves Herman/REUTERS

blocks.text: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney was addressing the European Parliament on Thursday, in a speech that focused on Canada's and the European Union's shared security and economic interests.
In an address in which Carney spoke in English, French and German, the Canadian prime minister lauded European culture and values of democracy, freedom and human rights, which he said Canada shares.

"We are not fair-weather allies. We do not pursue zero-sum deals. Our commitment to the rule of law, and our unyielding defense of human dignity, individual freedom and democracy share the same deep roots, the same unwavering dedication," the Canadian leader told the chamber, to applause.
Europe and Canada are 'stronger together', Carney tells EU Parliament
"We hold common values for which we have always fought and in whose defense we must always remain vigilant," he said.
Carney also said his country "welcomes" the "ambition" of the EU's proposal of an "associated membership".
"Europe and Canada are each strong," he said. But he added that "Europe and Canada are even stronger together."
"I am not proposing a third bloc in order to become a great-power rival — only with better manners,” he said. "We do not seek power to dominate others."
"The ​objective is not ⁠self-sufficiency, ​it's ​collective resilience", Carney ​said.
His speech to European lawmakers comes as the EU and Canada look to strengthen their ties amid a growing rift between Canada and its southern neighbor and main trading partner, the US.

Ties between Canada and the US have hit a historic low in recent months, with the North American neighbors locked in an escalating trade war since Carney and US President Donald Trump failed to agree on a deal this summer.
EU defends Canada alliance plan after Trump tariffs threat

On Wednesday, the European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said the EU was willing to make Canada its first-ever "associate member," days after the Wall Street Journal reported that Carney was exploring an "associate membership" with the bloc, a position that does not currently exist.

During her State of the EU address, von der Leyen said the bloc needed to adapt to an "openly hostile world" marked by aggressive power politics and "frayed relationships," the latter a clear nod to the turbulent ties between Brussels and Washington since Trump returned to the White House.
Prior to his visit this week, Carney had confirmed that he wanted to establish a "unique alliance" between Canada and the EU.
"We share the same values, we have the same priorities and ​we have very complementary strengths," the prime minister said.
Trump on Wednesday slammed the EU's plans to make Canada an associate member.

"If they do that, if I think it's at all a hostile act, I will put very serious tariffs or stop trading with Europe on many things," Trump told reporters en route to an event in North Carolina. The US president also described the prospect of Canada joining the EU as "laughable."
Carney: Canada to have talks with EU on 'unique alliance'
How did the US-Canada relationship come to this?
Ties between Canada and the US have plummeted since Trump began his second term in January 2025. He has targeted Canada with tariffs and suggested that the US could annex Canada as its 51st state.
Trump has also referred to Carney, as well as his predecessor as prime minister, Justin Trudeau, as the "governor" of Canada.
The growing rift has also seen Trump sign an executive order renaming Lake Ontario, a Great Lake between the US and Canada, to "Lake America."
As Trump menaces, some think Canada should join the EU

articles.title: [READOUT] Where businesses can plug into the Luzon Corridor
articles.summary: Of the initiative’s roughly $20 billion worth of disclosed opportunities, 99% are in transport, logistics, and energy projects, underscoring how much of the corridor’s high-tech potential still…

blocks.text: The government’s much-touted Luzon Economic Corridor (LEC) comes with an eye-catching number: about $20 billion (more than P1 trillion) worth of disclosed opportunities stretching across Subic, Clark, Metro Manila, and Batangas, if its investment dealbook is to be believed.
But for business leaders, that headline number may not be the most useful metric since the opportunities are scattered across different stages of development.

Rappler’s analysis, conducted alongside independent research analyst and strategic advisor Cesar Tolentino, found that less than $5.1 billion (P320.4 billion) of roughly $21.4 billion (P1.34 trillion) in identifiable project values could already be classified as pledged, being spent, implemented, or completed.

Much of the rest is still looking for investors, undergoing studies, or awaiting procurement. So rather than treating the corridor as $20 billion of investment that is definitely coming, it may be more useful to ask where your business can already plug in.
First, LEC is looking for much more than investors.
Rappler’s review of the 31 detailed opportunities shows that many projects are simultaneously seeking different kinds of private sector participation.

items: 27 identify opportunities for investors
24 are looking for suppliers
18 are seeking locators
A smaller number are explicitly looking for customers, offtakers, or other partners

blocks.text: That opens the corridor to companies beyond those interested in bankrolling an airport or railway. For instance, equipment providers could supply projects. Manufacturers and logistics firms could locate around new infrastructure. Operators could compete for long-term concessions. Energy users could become customers or offtakers.
Second, forget the government’s high-tech rhetoric for now. The near-term LEC opportunity is mostly about the basic infrastructure businesses need to operate.

Of the 31 projects, 17 are in transport and logistics and seven are in energy. There are only four digital connectivity projects and two classified under advanced manufacturing. In dollar terms, transport, logistics, and energy make up almost 99% of the pipeline with disclosed values.
That means the projects worth watching are mostly railways, ports, airports, power infrastructure, fuel pipelines, warehouses, and industrial facilities.

They may be less exciting than artificial intelligence or semiconductor design, but they are the investments that could eventually make Subic, New Clark City, and the country’s industrial parks more attractive to locators.
Third, pay attention to project stage, not just opportunity value.
Four huge opportunities account for around four-fifths of the dealbook’s disclosed value:

items: $4.1 billion (P257.6 billion) Sangley Point International Airport
$4 billion (P251.3 billion) North-South Commuter Railway operations and maintenance opportunity
$3 billion (P188.5 billion) Metro Manila Subway O&M concession
$3 billion to $6 billion (P188.5 billion to P377.0 billion) Subic-Clark natural gas ecosystem

blocks.text: But most other large projects remain years away. Studies for the proposed Subic-Clark-Manila-Batangas freight railway are expected to run until 2029, while Metro Manila Subway Phase 2 is also still undergoing feasibility work.

For businesses looking for nearer-term opportunities, the smaller projects may thus be more relevant. The Clark National Food Hub has already secured an initial $65 million (P4.08 billion). Civil works are complete for a $20-million to $25-million (P1.26-billion to P1.57-billion) insulated panel factory expansion in Pampanga, with equipment already in transit. Development of a $30-million (P1.88-billion) Subic fuel depot began in May.

The Philippines and United States also signed a separate $60-million (P3.77-billion) grant for energy sector reforms during the LEC forum. It may be nowhere near the size of the headline infrastructure pipeline, but crucially, it’s actual committed funding aimed at fixing one of the biggest constraints businesses face: high electricity costs.
Finally, treat the corridor’s high-tech ambitions as upside rather than the present reality.

The government wants New Clark City to eventually attract AI, semiconductor, and advanced manufacturing investments. But those industries barely appear in the pipeline today. Pax Silica itself is not among the dealbook’s detailed projects.

For now, LEC is overwhelmingly an infrastructure story. But rail, ports, power, logistics, and connectivity are exactly the foundations the Philippines needs before higher-value industries will commit capital.

No less than Finance Secretary Frederick Go told Rappler that advanced manufacturing, electronics, and AI-related tech “won’t be handed to us on a silver platter. We have to work hard to deserve it and become a global player in these industries.”
We hope this readout helps inform your next strategy or boardroom decision. And as always, feel free to tell us what to tackle next, dear business leader. – Rappler.com

Readout is a new content series from data consultancy The Nerve, bringing you insights that bridge the gap between quick news headlines and dense technical reports. Readout tracks and explains business shifts in different Philippine industries. Crafted from on-the-ground reporting and data-driven analyses, Readout provides a clear read on where market and consumption are headed, what’s shaping demand across different sectors, who the key players are, and why it all matters.

articles.title: New arrest, troubles delaying investigation into 2022 Manitoba smuggling deaths revealed in warrant documents
articles.summary: Newly obtained search warrant documents reveal police arrested a driver this year believed to have been involved in a human smuggling scheme that led to the deaths of a family of four in Manitoba in…

image.caption: A photo posted on Facebook in 2019 shows the Patel family: Jagdish, 39, Dharmik, 3, Vihangi, 11, and Vaishali, 37. They were found frozen to death in Manitoba, near the U.S. border, in January 2022. (Vaishali Patel/Facebook)

blocks.text: Manitoba·New

Newly obtained search warrant documents reveal police arrested a driver this year believed to have been involved in a human smuggling scheme that led to the deaths of a family of four in Manitoba in 2022.
Judge rules other information to remain redacted, citing 'serious risk' to RCMP investigation's integrity
The documents also provide a closer look into the years-long investigation — and shed light on some of the reasons why RCMP say it's taking so long.

It's been nearly five years since the frozen bodies of 39-year-old Jagdish Patel, his 37-year-old wife, Vaishali, and their two kids — 11-year-old Vihangi and three-year-old Dharmik — were found 12 metres from the U.S. border. They were trying to walk from Manitoba into Minnesota in January 2022 and became separated from a larger group of migrants.

In a trove of search warrant documents obtained by CBC News, RCMP said the unnamed driver arrested in February 2026 — one of the most recent updates made public in the case — is believed to have helped bring the Patels and other migrants to Winnipeg before their treacherous journey to the border.
"Investigation is ongoing to determine if they will be a witness or subject to prosecution in either Canada or the United States," an affidavit filed by an RCMP sergeant in May said.
The documents also paint a picture of why the RCMP say the investigation has progressed so slowly.

Though Canadian "person of interest" Fenil Patel — whom the documents allege was responsible for organizing the smuggling and drove the migrants to the border — was arrested last year after a U.S. extradition request, no charges in the investigation have been laid in Canada.
The Fifth Estate questions Fenil Patel
The RCMP affidavit from May 2026 said U.S. law enforcement told Mounties they'd gotten a sealed indictment for six charges against Patel, who is not related to the Patel family.

In the months before his arrest last year, an earlier affidavit filed by an RCMP constable said the unit responsible for border-related cases in Manitoba had been "plagued with resourcing challenges and competing priorities."

"Due to resourcing issues and deployments to the border beginning in January 2025 as a result of the recent spotlight on the international border by the new President of the USA, RCMP investigators have been unable to follow up on new developments of the Investigation," including search warrant results and information from U.S. Homeland Security Investigations, the May 2025 affidavit said.

items: Authorities feared man arrested in smuggling scheme that led to deaths at border would flee: court documents
Family called for help before freezing to death near Manitoba-U.S. border in 2022, smuggler testifies

blocks.text: The delays were also blamed on the relatively small border unit being responsible for newly reported human smuggling investigations that needed to be prioritized for prosecution, and on staff members not being immediately replaced after leaving the unit.

Though the documents reveal more about the case — including information about the Patel family's final days, details about Fenil Patel's alleged activities before their deaths and a 2025 reference to other potential "unidentified co-conspirators" — much of the information they contain remains redacted after a ruling from a Manitoba judge last week.
CBC News fought in court to unseal the search warrant documents, including the unredacted portions.
Provincial court Judge Tracey Lord found disclosing the redacted information "would create a serious risk to the integrity of the ongoing investigation.
"While the investigative decisions left to be made in this case are few at this stage, they are nonetheless significant in terms of how or if the case may proceed," Lord wrote.
Some identities remain unknown: documents
As RCMP investigated the case, they applied for more than 40 warrants for everything from bank and phone records to information about car rentals and email accounts, the documents said.

That investigation also included details provided by people who interacted with the Patel family in their final days, including the manager of a hotel where the family stayed in Mississauga, Ont., an acquaintance they stayed with in Welland, Ont., and an Uber driver who gave them a ride in-between.

The Welland acquaintance, whom the documents said grew up with Jagdish Patel in Gujarat, India, later gave the family a ride to another Mississauga hotel, where he said he saw two men meet them outside.

items: Man accused of smuggling migrant family who froze to death at border arrested, Canadian authorities say
New details revealed about days Indian family spent in Ontario before freezing to death near U.S. border

blocks.text: "The identity of these 2 males remains unknown," the documents said.

The documents also said the Patel family was in Canada on a visitor's visa that named a Mississauga woman as the person they were visiting. That woman later told police she didn't know the Patels or why her name was on their documents "and was concerned that her identity had been stolen," the documents said.
The other migrants who travelled with them were issued work or study permits, or both.

"Information received from [from the Canada Border Services Agency] indicated that the [visas] obtained by these Indian [nationals] were done so via fraudulent documents, such as student records and providing false visitor names," the documents said.
Booking hotel rooms back to 2018
Police also spoke to two managers at a hotel where the Patel family stayed, who recognized a photo of Fenil Patel as a man who would book rooms for people he said were students, the documents said.

One of the managers said Patel had once mentioned to her that "he had an agency 'back home' and that was how he was bringing the students into Canada," while the other said she remembered him booking hotel rooms as far back as 2018.
The students would stay for anywhere between a day and over a week, paying on a day-by-day basis.

items: 'I was very scared,' migrant who survived crossing border in blizzard says at human smuggling trial
Migrants 'nothing but dollar signs' to accused human smugglers, U.S. prosecutors say in closing arguments

blocks.text: "When asked about who the people were, he simply stated that they were students from India who did not have a place to live and he was looking for accommodations for them," the documents said.
Fenil Patel remains in custody in Canada and is scheduled to appear in court next month for a disclosure application in his extradition case, court records show.

Two men convicted in the U.S. for their roles in the smuggling operation were handed lengthy prison sentences last year. Steve Shand and Harshkumar Patel, who is also not related to the Patel family, have both filed appeals.

articles.title: Ninth woman's body found as South African police investigate string of deaths
articles.summary: South Africa police have cautioned against assuming that all the killings are linked but many women are afraid.

blocks.text: Police in South Africa have confirmed the discovery of a ninth woman's body in just two months, amid growing concern over a string of unexplained deaths east of Johannesburg.
The latest victim was found half-naked and wrapped in a sheet on the side of a road in Dawn Park on Thursday morning, police said. Her identity has not yet been released.
The discovery follows the deaths of eight other women whose bodies have been found since July across Ekurhuleni, a major urban area of Johannesburg.

Several of the women were found partially clothed and with injuries, but police have stressed that they have not established whether all the deaths are connected or whether a serial killer is responsible.
President Cyril Ramaphosa has vowed that "no stone will be left unturned" in finding those behind the killings, which he said were "causing fear and uncertainty in our communities".

Among the victims was 38-year-old Elizabeth "Tsontso" Moselakgomo, who disappeared last week after leaving her home for an afternoon run. Her body was found three days later behind a hotel in Kempton Park.

Two other victims have since been identified as Itumeleng Kekana, who had been missing since July, and 38-year-old Dineo Evelyn Motapane, whose body was discovered by the roadside in KwaThema on Tuesday.

The first of the nine bodies was discovered in Kempton Park on 15 July. A suspect was arrested two days later in connection with that case and remains in custody, but police have not linked that suspect to the other deaths.
Further bodies were discovered in August and September, including in Kempton Park, Olifantsfontein, Clayville and KwaThema.
The latest body is of a woman believed to be in her 30s and appeared to have bruises and stab wounds, local media reported.

Police have assembled a multidisciplinary team of detectives, intelligence officers, forensic experts and other specialists to investigate the deaths and establish whether there are links between the cases.
They are also pursuing a person of interest, although they have not disclosed which case or cases that person may be connected to.
"Let's not get emotional, the gloves are off," said Gauteng Premier Panyaza Lesufi on Thursday, adding that the authorities had the capacity to deal with the killings.

Authorities have offered a 400,000 rand ($24,000; £18,000) reward for information that could lead to arrests and have appealed to families with missing relatives to help identify the remaining victims.

The discoveries have caused widespread alarm in Ekurhuleni, particularly around Kempton Park, and come against the backdrop of longstanding concern about high levels of violence against women in South Africa.
Police say they are not linking the deaths to a serial killer at this stage, but are investigating the possibility that a group of people is behind the killings.
Acting Police Minister Firoz Cachalia has cautioned against speculation, saying investigators were dealing with what appeared, at this stage, to be "quite distinct, separate events".

articles.title: Gov't work on September 28 suspended starting 1 p.m. for National Family Week
articles.summary: Malacañang on Thursday suspended government work on September 28, starting at 1 p.m. to commemorate the 34th National Family Week.

blocks.text: Published September 17, 2026 5:51pm
Malacañang on Thursday suspended government work on September 28, starting at 1 p.m. to commemorate the 34th National Family Week.

This is in line with Proclamation 60, series of 1992, which declared the last week of September every year as Family Week. It also follows Proclamation 326, series of 2012 which declared the fourth Monday of every September as the “Kainang Pamilya Mahalaga" Day.

“Work in all agencies and instrumentalities of the National Government, including government-owned or -controlled corporations and state universities and colleges, shall be suspended on 28 September 2026 starting 1:00 in the afternoon.” Executive Secretary Ralph Recto said in Memorandum Circular 136.
However, government agencies whose functions involve the delivery of basic and health services and disaster response will continue their operations.
The Palace order also encouraged government workers in the executive branch to support activities in relation to National Family Week.

“The suspension of work in other branches of government, independent commissions or bodies, and the private sector is also encouraged to afford all Filipino families the full opportunity to celebrate the 34th National Family Week,” Recto wrote in the order.
The memorandum circular was signed on Wednesday but released to the public on Thursday. —Jean Mangaluz/LDF, GMA News

articles.title: DFA alarmed by Israel's West Bank settlement plan, says it could violate int'l law
articles.summary: The Department of Foreign Affairs (DFA) on Thursday expressed alarm over the Israeli government's settlement plan in the West Bank, citing it could violate international law.

blocks.text: Published September 17, 2026 5:50pm
The Department of Foreign Affairs (DFA) on Thursday expressed alarm over the Israeli government's settlement plan in the West Bank, citing it could violate international law.

“We express our deep concern over recent developments in the West Bank. We note with alarm the efforts of the Israeli government to advance the E1 settlement plan as well as the continued rise of settler violence in the West Bank,” the DFA said in a statement.
“The Philippines views these actions, which may contravene international law, as detrimental to finding a just, lasting and comprehensive solution to the Middle East conflict,” it added.
The DFA also urged all parties to refrain from unilateral actions that could undermine peace efforts and prospects for a future Palestinian state.
“The Philippines remains resolute in upholding the fundamental and legitimate rights of the Palestinian people, in particular the right to self-determination,” the department said.
The DFA made the statement that came after Israel approved a major new settlement project in the West Bank.
Tel Aviv plans to build over 1,200 homes under the East 1 (E1) settlement—projects to expand its Ma’ale Adumim settlement and connect it to Jerusalem. —Mariel Celine Serquiña/RF, GMA News

articles.title: 911 service down across Ontario and parts of Canada
articles.summary: Access to 911 service is down across parts of Canada and Ontario, including in Toronto, Waterloo and Winnipeg, according to emergency response services.

image.caption: 911 service is down across many parts of Ontario and in some cities across Canada on Thursday morning. (Michael Wilson/CBC)

blocks.text: Toronto·Breaking
Access to 911 service is down across parts of Canada and Ontario, including in Toronto, Waterloo and Winnipeg, according to emergency response services.
Anyone in need of 911 urged to contact non-emergency lines
Residents in need of emergency services and unable to contact 911 are being urged to contact any available non-emergency lines.

All emergency services in Toronto, Durham Region and Ontario Provincial Police services across the provinces shared on social media platform X that they are still experiencing an outage of their 911 services as of 5:40 a.m. Thursday.
But police in York and Peel region in the Greater Toronto Area, shared on X that their service is now back up and running.
Bell 911 service is down across Ontario, a spokesperson with Toronto paramedics told CBC News.
They said typically 911 calls are filtered and transferred by dispatchers with the Toronto police.
How to reach Toronto emergency services
Toronto paramedics said anyone needing their assistance Thursday morning should still call 911, as some calls have still been coming through this morning.
Toronto police shared on X that anyone needing emergency assistance should reach out to their non-emergency line at 416-808-2222 or directly contact their local division.
Toronto Fire said on X they can be contacted through their non-emergency line at 416-338-9000.
More to come.

articles.title: Marcoleta won't ask court to let him participate in VP Sara impeachment trial
articles.summary: Senator Rodante Marcoleta on Thursday said he won"t ask the Sandiganbayan Third Division to allow him to participate in the impeachment trial of his ally, Vice President Sara Duterte.

blocks.text: Published September 17, 2026 5:24pm
Senator Rodante Marcoleta on Thursday said he won’t ask the Sandiganbayan Third Division to allow him to participate in the impeachment trial of his ally, Vice President Sara Duterte.

Asked if he would file a petition to be allowed to participate in the trial, Marcoleta said that there is no use participating in the proceedings, which he said is “illegitimately” presided by Senate impeachment court presiding officer Francis “Chiz” Escudero.

“They [Senate] did not take up my manifestation because I was questioning, first of all, the legitimacy of the presiding officer. The last time I checked, it should be the Senate President who will preside. So kung hindi nila ita-take up iyon, bakit pa ako mag-participate doon?” Marcoleta said on the sidelines of the hearing on his pending bail petition in connection with the plunder charge leveled against him over P75 million in undeclared campaign contributions.
(So if they're not going to take it up, why would I participate in there?)

Marcoleta was referring to his July 20 written manifestation before the Senate impeachment court, which argued that it should be the Senate President to preside over the Senate court as provided by the Impeachment Rules.

“They have not even discussed, they have not even debated the merits of my manifestation and request. I'm hoping that you will discuss this and it will be taken up and deemed to be part of the proceedings of the Senate. Wala man lang,” he said.

The Senate, however, amended Rule 2 of its Rules of Impeachment ahead of the start of the impeachment trial of the Vice President which now states that “The President of the Senate shall preside in all other cases of impeachment unless the Senate, by a majority vote of the members present, elects another Senator as the Presiding Officer.”

Senator Jinggoy Estrada, who is also detained and facing a P573-million plunder and graft charges over alleged links to the flood control scam, had asked Sandiganbayan to allow him to participate in the impeachment trial. It was denied by the anti-graft court for lack of merit.
Threshold
Be that as it may, Marcoleta said that the voting threshold for conviction of an impeachable official is at 16 or two-third of the 24 members of the Senate.
“You will ask me why? I don't think the threshold is a subject of votation. It's already in the Constitution. Nobody has the right to change the language of the Constitution,” Marcoleta said.

“The Constitution says that no person should be adjudged guilty without the concurrence of two-thirds of all the members of the Senate. That's it. It is as simple as that. Why should it be a subject of votation? Are you questioning the language of the Constitution?” Marcoleta added.

A day before, former Chief Justices of the Supreme Court Hilario Davide, Jr., Artemio Panganiban and Reynato Puno all said before the Senate impeachment court that the Constitutional provision stating that two-thirds of all the members of the Senate are needed to secure a conviction does not mean 16 must automatically be the threshold for conviction.

The former SC Chief Justices shared their thoughts before the court as amici curiae, or “friends of the court," to answer the Senator judges' queries on the threshold for conviction amid the continued absence of at least four of the 24 senator-judges in the proceedings, including Marcoleta.

In arguing their position, Davide, Jr., Panganiban and Puno cited the Senate’s authority to try and decide impeachment cases and a “a strict, standalone, literal interpretation may result in absurdities and may result in injustices which will defeat the purpose of the Constitution.”
It was only retired Supreme Court Associate Justice Adolf Azcuna who said every member of the Senate should be counted in determining the threshold for conviction. — BM, GMA News

articles.title: Macalintal asks Marcos to veto 5-year term for barangay, SK officials
articles.summary: Election lawyer Romulo Macalintal on Thursday asked President Ferdinand "Bongbong" Marcos Jr. to veto the measure seeking to "fix" the term of office of barangay officials and members of the…

blocks.text: Published September 17, 2026 5:24pm

Election lawyer Romulo Macalintal on Thursday asked President Ferdinand "Bongbong" Marcos Jr. to veto the measure seeking to "fix" the term of office of barangay officials and members of the Sangguniang Kabataan (SK) to five years.
In his letter, Macalintal said the measure "will inflict severe constitutional injury upon our democratic framework.”

He pointed out that it is a direct violation of the electorate’s right of suffrage, as “postponing elections and extending the terms of sitting officials through legislative fiat effectively supplants the sovereign will of the people.”
Macalintal added that Congress, during its hearings, has only invited barangay officials, who would naturally support the measure.
“Hence, this letter-petition includes our prayer for a personal audience with Your Excellency and your legal advisers to be heard on this matter,” he said.

The election lawyer also described as “flimsy” the reasons cited for extending the terms of office of barangay officials and Sangguniang Kabataan members, including an alleged “oil crisis,” foreign wars, and funding concerns.
He added that the Commission on Elections (Comelec) has publicly and repeatedly expressed its readiness to conduct the Barangay and Sangguniang Kabataan Elections (BSKE).

Macalintal further said the measure violates Article VI, Section 26 (1) of the 1987 Philippine Constitution, which states that “every bill passed by the Congress shall embrace only one subject which shall be expressed in the title thereof.”
“While deceptively titled as an act "fixing" the term of office, the body of the statute sweeps broadly to cancel ongoing electoral timeline, extent tenures, and impose hold-overs,” he said.
The lawyer pointed out that if the proposed measure aims to adjust future terms of office, any new term structure should apply to officials elected in the November 2, 2026 polls.
“That less restrictive path would have fulfilled term-setting goals without trampling upon the lectorate's fundamental right to choose their grassroots leaders,” Macalintal said.
GMA News Online has reached out to Malacañang and Comelec for comment on the matter.
On Monday, the Senate approved on third and final reading a bill seeking to "fix" the term of office of barangay officials and SK members to five years.
With 13 affirmative votes, five negative votes, and no abstentions, the upper chamber approved Senate Bill No. 2387 during its plenary session.

The measure seeks to amend Republic Act No. 12232 by fixing the current four-year term of barangay and SK officials to five years and moving the next BSKE from the first to the second Monday of November 2028.

It also provides that no elective barangay official shall serve for more than two consecutive terms in the same position, while no elective SK official shall serve for more than one term in the same position.

Senator Francis “Chiz” Escudero, the measure’s principal author and sponsor, said the five-year term would give barangay and SK officials more time to plan, implement, and evaluate programs before the next elections.
Earlier this month, the House of Representatives approved its version of the bill. —AOL, GMA News
